mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each week for the last four weeks (-1.6 to 0.3). This monotonic momentum reflects an ongoing recovery in discretionary outings that should persist, producing a higher 4-week mean of RETAIL_REC going forward.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose each week from -1.6 to 0.3 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days despite the observed four-week upward streak.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses and holds above 0.5 percent-change-from-baseline for two consecutive weeks, it signals a durable return of commuting and errand trips that mechanically feeds adjacent retail footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean exceeds 0.5 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly means are 0.7, 0.6, 0.6 over the last three weeks, hovering near the 0.5 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the subsequent two weeks even though TRANSIT has stayed above 0.5 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both trend upward simultaneously, the combined effect of more commuting and more in-office work amplifies lunchtime and after-work retail visits beyond what either series alone would predict, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from 3.9 to 4.3 and TRANSIT rose from -0.1 to 0.6 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days even when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show simultaneous week-on-week increases across the period.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has plateaued at an elevated level (~43-44) for four weeks, indicating households are still prioritizing essential errands over discretionary retail, consistent with lingering cautious behavior under partial restrictions, which caps RETAIL_REC growth.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within 42.9-44.4 for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat at an elevated plateau, indicating no suppressive link.

mechanism_narrative: Hong Kong's cooler autumn/winter weather drives a seasonal rise in outdoor PARKS activity (from -10.6 to -6.7 over four weeks), which substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits, dampening RETAIL_REC over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved steadily from -10.6 to -6.7 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days in tandem with continued PARKS increases, showing no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed flat and elevated (around 3.7-4.0) for four weeks, indicating a persistent home-centric routine (e.g., partial remote work) that limits the time available for retail and recreation trips in the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL held between 3.7 and 4.0 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 7 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining flat and elevated, indicating no suppressive relationship.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility reverses and drops below -10 (its t-3w level) within a week, it signals reduced outdoor substitution activity, and that freed-up discretionary time should redirect toward retail and recreation visits within a week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS has been improving from -10.6 toward -6.7, so a reversal below -10 would be a notable regime change
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop below -10, or PARKS never crosses that threshold during the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES would indicate broader relaxation of restrictions affecting both essential and office activity, and this joint policy-driven loosening should spill over to boost RETAIL_REC within two weeks beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from 3.9 to 4.3 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed near 43-44 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 14 days even when both GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES increase together week-on-week.
